Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the candid discussion. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Performance targets you confirmed: 95th pct latency <= 120ms for single-stream token generation (prompt+first 64 tokens), sustain 12 qps steady-state, burst to 50 qps for 2-3 minutes. You also called out streaming requirements for live search snippets (sub-50ms first-token preferred).

2) Workload shape: mixture of short prompts (avg 80 tokens total) for search snippets (~60% of traffic) and longer generation tasks for summarization (~40%). Concurrency: typical concurrency 10-15 users, peak concurrent requests ~35.

3) Immediate ask from your infra team: an initial dedicated capacity sizing recommendation (GPU type options + reserved throughput) so you can budget for a pilot.

Action items I propose: 
- Redwood to deliver a concise capacity-fit memo with two price-performance options (NVidia H100 vs A800-like equivalence) and recommended reserved throughput (qps + concurrent slots) by EOD Monday. 
- Schedule a 30-min technical sync with your infra folks (please suggest times).
- Share the minimal test prompts and 1-week traffic sample for a short perf replay.

I'll attach a compact SLO/throughput matrix and an initial sizing note — these are preliminary and will be validated in a short bench run.

Thanks,

Ben / team — attaching the quick capacity-fit note you requested (redwood-dedicated-sizing-notes.pdf) and a compact SLO matrix spreadsheet. Highlights / my high-level recommendation below: 

- Summary constraints: 95th <= 120ms for snippets, 95th <= 300ms for summarization; steady-state 12 qps, burst 50 qps for 5 minutes; average request ~80 tokens (prompt+response).

- Option A (Cost-Optimized): A800-equivalent nodes, reservation plan: 2x A800 nodes (N=2) with autoscale headroom for bursts using spot/dynamic pool. Expected steady throughput ~14 qps with batching, estimated 95th pct for snippets ~110-140ms depending on batching aggressiveness (risk: tail spikes). Monthly reserved cost estimate included in PDF.

- Option B (Latency-Optimized): H100-equivalent nodes, reservation plan: 1x H100 + 1x H100 standby (N=2) with pre-warmed KV cache and streaming-optimized runtime. Expected steady throughput ~18 qps with lower latency headroom; 95th pct for snippets ~70-100ms, much tighter first-token for streaming (<40ms achievable). Higher monthly cost, but more predictable tail behavior.

- Concurrency guidance: reserve concurrency slots to cap per-request token queues — recommend reserving 40 concurrent slots to cover peaks and avoid queue amplification during the 5-minute burst.

- Validation plan: small-scale bench run using your sample workload to validate 95th pct and streaming first-byte times. We'll run three 30-minute windows (steady, ramp, burst) and produce a short validation report. Aim to run week of 3/22 if your team approves.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Ben: share the formal quote for both options and high-level TCO.
2) Samantha: confirm the Tuesday technical sync or propose alternate.
3) Infra: drop the 3-day traffic CSV and sample prompts in Drive.

Marissa
